provenance.description: M3b first connected picking/packing slice: 6 small burst orders on the accepted main-warehouse geometry/stock/products/resources/units; no inbound deliveries; finite-cohort run for SUPPORTED_STAGE_COMPLETE.
assumptions: Derived from fixtures/operations/main-warehouse.json sha256 c6e4f208835e31de2554850fa618953bb6f9a1b03c360b137c784bd5112660cb (23520 bytes), cargo-c2 model: room, racks, obstacles, products, locations, initial stock, home assignments, mobile units (4 pickers + 2 putaway), and all resource coordinates/capacities/durations are unchanged FROM THE PARENT (the historical ce33a9c5/70ec57ab revision pair is preserved in oracles/git history, never rewritten).

Constructed fields: id, seed, provenance, orderSchedule (6 burst orders B-01..B-06 at 0/5000/10000/15000/20000/25000ms, 3-4 items each, single-trip loads), empty deliverySchedule, finite-cohort run with arrivalCutoffMs 25000.

Why this fixture exists: the full 28-order + 12-delivery main schedule is NOT executable as the M3b slice (inbound unsupported); this burst proves scheduled orders -> reservations -> concurrent picks -> packing queues -> READY_FOR_DISPATCH on real main-warehouse coordinates.

Simplifications: no inbound deliveries; putaway units stay idle at occupied parking; packing service uses the configured 90000ms durations; pick/unload handling durations come from the saved execution runconfig, not the scenario.
Both PACK-1 and PACK-2 run as configured (1 lane each); queue waits arise from the 90s service under the 6-order burst, not from hardcoded metrics.

Cargo-C2: centered 680x1220+100 (r799) profile, capacity 4 (2 equipment crates x 2 fixed cells); all 6 burst orders are 3-4 items in unchanged single-trip lines; PACK2-Q3 at (20500,9400); 6/6 READY proven on this geometry with the consistent disc-occupancy planner.
inventedFields: burst order ids, arrivals, and quantities; run mode and cutoff

baseline.decisionCriterion: Pareto over available fields: shipped (higher better), makespanMs (lower better, complete cohorts only), lastShippedAtMs (lower better, within-window timing only, never a completion claim), totalWaitMs (lower better), backlog (lower better). Better somewhere and worse nowhere = improved; the mirror = worse; both directions = mixed; all equal = no-improvement.
assumptions: synthetic scenario inputs are constructed test inputs, not calibrated measurements
baseline and candidate share identical orders, deliveries, initial stock, seed, worker profiles/count, service durations and execution config; only the moved station's attached coordinates differ
an invalid candidate returns no measured performance; worse, mixed and no-improvement candidates are retained honestly
